# Subalgebras generated by homogeneous submodules

The module `PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.HomogeneousGenerators`, [PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean): 17 declarations, 15 with a docstring.

## i. Overview

> Let `f : B →ₐ[R] B[X]` be an algebra map into the polynomials over a possibly
> noncommutative algebra `B`. The degree-`w` part of a subalgebra `A` is the submodule
> `A.homogeneousSubmodule f w` of elements `x ∈ A` with `f x = monomial w x`. Nothing
> requires `f` to be a grading of `B`: the pieces need not span `B`, and `f x` need not
> determine `x`.
>
> Suppose that `A` is generated by a family of submodules `D n`, and that `f` is the monomial
> `X ^ deg n` on `D n`. Then the degree-`w` part of `A` is spanned by the products
> `D n₁ * ⋯ * D nₖ`, in every order of the factors, whose degrees add up to `w`
> (`homogeneousSubmodule_eq_productsOfDegree`). The empty product is `1`, so degree zero
> contains the scalars. This is a spanning statement. It gives no unique decomposition, and
> it assumes neither that the generators commute nor that their products are nonzero.
>
> Everything else is read off from it.
>
> - Removing the leftmost factor of each product: the degree-`w` part, for `w` positive, is
>   spanned by the products `D k * A_(w - deg k)` (`homogeneousSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul`). This
>   needs no positivity. When some `deg k` vanishes, the right-hand side contains the term
>   `D k * A_w` of the same degree, so the equality holds without giving a decreasing
>   recursion.
> - If every generator has positive degree, degree zero is exactly the scalar submodule `1`
>   (`homogeneousSubmodule_zero_eq_one`), the image of `R` in `B`, which need not be a copy
>   of `R`.
> - If moreover `n < deg n`, the degree-`i` part is spanned by the generators of degree `i`
>   and the products of two parts of smaller positive degree
>   (`homogeneousSubmodule_eq_sup_iSup_mul`). The bound makes the index ranges finite.
> - A property of degrees holding at zero and at every generator degree, and closed under
>   addition, holds at every degree with a nonzero part (`homogeneousSubmodule_eq_bot`).
>   This only proves vanishing: a degree with the property may still have zero part.

## ii. Key results

> - `Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule` : the degree-`w` part of a subalgebra.
> - `Submodule.productsOfDegree` : the span of the products of generators of total degree `w`.
> - `Subalgebra.coeff_mem_homogeneousSubmodule` : the coefficients of `f x` are homogeneous.
> - `Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_productsOfDegree` : spanning by products.
> - `Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul` : removing the leftmost generator.
> - `Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_zero_eq_one` : degree zero is the scalars.
> - `Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_sup_iSup_mul` : the binary recursion.
> - `Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_bot` : unreachable degrees vanish.

## A. The homogeneous submodules of a subalgebra

**`Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule`**, a def, [line 86](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L86).

> The degree-`w` part of `A` for `f`: the elements `x ∈ A` with `f x = monomial w x`.

```lean
noncomputable def homogeneousSubmodule (A : Subalgebra R B) (f : B →ₐ[R] Polynomial B)
    (w : ℕ) : Submodule R B
```

**`Subalgebra.mem_homogeneousSubmodule_iff`**, a lemma, [line 94](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L94).

```lean
lemma mem_homogeneousSubmodule_iff {w : ℕ} {x : B} :
    x ∈ A.homogeneousSubmodule f w ↔ x ∈ A ∧ f x = Polynomial.monomial w x
```

**`Subalgebra.one_le_homogeneousSubmodule_zero`**, a lemma, [line 101](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L101).

> The scalars have degree zero.

```lean
lemma one_le_homogeneousSubmodule_zero : (1 : Submodule R B) ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f 0
```

**`Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_mul_le`**, a lemma, [line 105](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L105).

> Degrees add under multiplication.

```lean
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_mul_le (m n : ℕ) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f m * A.homogeneousSubmodule f n
      ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f (m + n)
```

## B. Products of generators of a given total degree

**`Submodule.productsOfDegree`**, a def, [line 126](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L126).

> The span of the products `D n₁ * ⋯ * D nₖ` whose degrees `deg n₁ + ⋯ + deg nₖ` add up
> to `w`. Every order of the factors occurs separately, and the empty product is `1`.

```lean
noncomputable def productsOfDegree (D : ℕ → Submodule R B) (deg : ℕ → ℕ) (w : ℕ) :
    Submodule R B
```

**`Submodule.list_prod_le_productsOfDegree`**, a lemma, [line 132](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L132).

```lean
lemma list_prod_le_productsOfDegree (l : List ℕ) :
    (l.map D).prod ≤ productsOfDegree D deg (l.map deg).sum
```

**`Submodule.productsOfDegree_mul_le`**, a lemma, [line 138](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L138).

> Concatenating products adds their degrees.

```lean
lemma productsOfDegree_mul_le (a b : ℕ) :
    productsOfDegree D deg a * productsOfDegree D deg b ≤ productsOfDegree D deg (a + b)
```

## C. Subalgebras generated by homogeneous submodules

> Throughout, `A` is generated by the submodules `D n` (`hA`), and `f` is the monomial
> `X ^ deg n` on `D n` (`hD`).

### C.1. Generators and coefficients

**`Subalgebra.le_homogeneousSubmodule`**, a lemma, [line 180](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L180).

> A generator in `D n` has degree `deg n`.

```lean
lemma le_homogeneousSubmodule (n : ℕ) : D n ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f (deg n)
```

**`Subalgebra.list_prod_le_homogeneousSubmodule`**, a lemma, [line 186](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L186).

> A product of generators has the sum of their degrees.

```lean
lemma list_prod_le_homogeneousSubmodule (l : List ℕ) :
    (l.map D).prod ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f (l.map deg).sum
```

**`Subalgebra.productsOfDegree_le_homogeneousSubmodule`**, a lemma, [line 197](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L197).

> The products of generators of total degree `w` lie in the degree-`w` part of `A`.

```lean
lemma productsOfDegree_le_homogeneousSubmodule (w : ℕ) :
    productsOfDegree D deg w ≤ A.homogeneousSubmodule f w
```

**`Subalgebra.coeff_mem_productsOfDegree`**, a lemma, [line 204](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L204).

> Every coefficient of `f x`, for `x ∈ A`, is a sum of products of generators: the one
> induction over the generation of `A`.

```lean
lemma coeff_mem_productsOfDegree {x : B} (hx : x ∈ A) (m : ℕ) :
    (f x).coeff m ∈ productsOfDegree D deg m
```

**`Subalgebra.coeff_mem_homogeneousSubmodule`**, a lemma, [line 231](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L231).

> The coefficient of `X ^ m` in `f x`, for `x ∈ A`, lies in the degree-`m` part of `A`.

```lean
lemma coeff_mem_homogeneousSubmodule {x : B} (hx : x ∈ A) (m : ℕ) :
    (f x).coeff m ∈ A.homogeneousSubmodule f m
```

### C.2. Spanning by products of generators

**`Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_productsOfDegree`**, a lemma, [line 244](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L244).

> The degree-`w` part of `A` is spanned by the products of generators, in every order,
> whose degrees add up to `w`.

```lean
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_eq_productsOfDegree (w : ℕ) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f w = productsOfDegree D deg w
```

### C.3. Removing the leftmost generator

**`Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul`**, a lemma, [line 260](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L260).

> For positive `w`, the degree-`w` part of `A` is spanned by the products of a generator
> `D k` of degree at most `w` with the part of the remaining degree. The bound `n ≤ deg n`
> only makes the range of `k` finite.

```lean
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_eq_iSup_mul (hle : ∀ n, n ≤ deg n) {w : ℕ} (hw : 0 < w) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f w
      = ⨆ k ∈ (Finset.range (w + 1)).filter (fun k => deg k ≤ w),
          D k * A.homogeneousSubmodule f (w - deg k)
```

### C.4. Degree zero and the binary recursion

**`Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_zero_eq_one`**, a lemma, [line 289](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L289).

> If every generator has positive degree, degree zero is the scalar submodule.

```lean
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_zero_eq_one (hpos : ∀ n, 0 < deg n) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f 0 = 1
```

**`Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_sup_iSup_mul`**, a lemma, [line 306](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L306).

> If `n < deg n` for every `n`, the degree-`i` part of `A`, for positive `i`, is spanned
> by the generators of degree `i` and the products of two parts of positive degrees adding
> up to `i`. It follows from removing the leftmost generator: a generator of degree `i`
> leaves degree zero, which is the scalars.

```lean
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_eq_sup_iSup_mul (hlt : ∀ n, n < deg n) (i : ℕ) (hi : 0 < i) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f i
      = (⨆ k ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun k : Fin i => deg k = i), D k)
        ⊔ (⨆ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : Fin i × Fin i => (p.1 : ℕ) + (p.2 : ℕ) = i),
            A.homogeneousSubmodule f p.1 * A.homogeneousSubmodule f p.2)
```

### C.5. Unreachable degrees

**`Subalgebra.homogeneousSubmodule_eq_bot`**, a lemma, [line 338](https://github.com/leanprover-community/physlib/blob/2a1dfe43134b49b643642f13d33031754021bb5d/PhyslibAlpha/Mathematics/HomogeneousGenerators.lean#L338).

> If a set of degrees contains `0` and every `deg n` and is closed under addition, a
> degree outside it has zero part. This proves vanishing only: a degree in the set may
> still have zero part.

```lean
lemma homogeneousSubmodule_eq_bot (P : ℕ → Prop) (h0 : P 0) (hP : ∀ n, P (deg n))
    (hadd : ∀ a b, P a → P b → P (a + b)) {w : ℕ} (hw : ¬ P w) :
    A.homogeneousSubmodule f w = ⊥
```
